No forbid-listed file (error.rs, pools.rs, migraciones.rs, any Cargo.toml, migrations dir) or hexcell-core/src/similitud.rs changed in this commit. (a) PURE AND SOLE COMPARISON SITE: decidir_motivo_semantico takes only value arguments (Option<f32>, i64, f32), performs no I/O, and is genuinely pure. Grepped the whole file for every occurrence of `umbral` and `is_finite`: the only place `sim < umbral_de_aceptacion` (or any threshold comparison) executes is inside this helper (line ~370). The approval branch only checks motivos.is_empty() && sim.is_finite() && metadatos.is_some() -- it never itself compares against the threshold, it just trusts that the helper already would have populated motivos if the threshold check failed. Confirmed: the extraction is real, not cosmetic.

(b) CANTIDAD HONESTY: for the single-bad-row case there is no double count -- the loop's match is mutually exclusive per row (a row either takes the Some(similitud) arm and can become mejor_similitud, or the None arm and increments incomparables; never both), so the +1 correctly accounts for the one row holding the poisoned maximum, which was never counted in incomparables. HOWEVER, in a hypothetical multi-corruption scenario (only reachable if a FUTURE similitud_coseno regressed to leak non-finite values again -- today's similitud_coseno already filters these into the None/incomparables path, making this whole branch unreachable via the real loop) the count would UNDERSTATE: NaN > NaN is always false, so once a non-finite value claims mejor_similitud, later non-finite rows can neither displace it (silently lost) nor fall into the None/incomparables arm (they took the Some arm). Two or more bad rows would still report cantidad = incomparables + 1, one short of the truth. This is a real precision gap in a diagnostic count, but it cannot cause a false approval (the verdict is still Rechazado) and is unreachable through the current, already-hardened similitud_coseno -- a note, not a blocker.

(c) REDUNDANCY IS GENUINELY DEAD, NOT DIVERGENT: decidir_motivo_semantico is the only caller path into a decision on mejor_similitud, and by exhaustive case analysis its match arms guarantee that whenever it returns None (no motivo pushed), the underlying sim was already finite (the non-finite arm is checked first and would have matched otherwise). So whenever the approval branch is reached with motivos.is_empty() and Some(sim), sim.is_finite() is always true given the current single call site -- the redundant check cannot fire today. If a future refactor ever let it fire, the fallback is Rechazado{motivos: []} (an unreasoned but fail-closed rejection), never a different motive or an approval -- worse cosmetically than a named reason, but never a false Aprobado. Verdict: real redundancy, correctly fail-closed, not a diverging behavior.

(d) BOTH TESTS MEANINGFUL, NEITHER INCIDENTAL: un_maximo_no_finito_se_rechaza_en_lugar_de_aprobarse is load-bearing per the orchestrator's own mutation (confirmed by inspection of the match arms too: flipping `!sim.is_finite()` to `false` routes NaN into the `Some(_) => None` arm, silently approving). una_similitud_finita_por_encima_del_umbral_no_produce_motivo does not exercise the SimilitudInsuficiente branch (that path is already covered externally by tests/validacion.rs AC-6 assertions at line ~498) but is not incidental either: it guards against an inverted or overly-aggressive finiteness check that would wrongly reject a comfortably-high, perfectly finite similarity -- a mutation that swaps the first arm's guard to `sim.is_finite()` would make exactly this test fail. Narrow but genuine.
